subject: Sequenced backup handoff for subprocessor rotation — retention & log exception asks
messages:
From: Aaron Lee <support@cloudbridge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: backup migration window for upcoming subprocessor rotation

Hi Mina —

Quick context: CloudBridge will rotate a storage subprocessor (S3 provider) for our EU region on the weekend of July 24–26. Our procurement and security teams want to coordinate with Redwood on retention guarantees and the exact timeline for backup snapshot retention, purge windows, and any log retention carve-outs so we can update our DPA addendum.

Key asks up front:
- What is the standard snapshot retention for full backups and incremental logs for EU customers?
- Can Redwood provide a temporary log-retention exception (audit logs) for this migration period and an escrow/archive for 180 days if we need for regulatory review?
- What does the deletion workflow look like if we need to rollback (who authorizes, how long before deletion becomes irreversible)?

We attached our migration plan for reference (cloudbridge_subproc_rotation_v1.pdf). Would appreciate a short meeting next week with your ops and compliance folks to lock the windows and any DPA redlines. Marcus — looping you in for ops constraints.

Thanks,
Aaron Lee
Sr. Cloud Ops — CloudBridge
attachments: cloudbridge_subproc_rotation_v1.pdf

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <support@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: backup migration window for upcoming subprocessor rotation

Aaron — thanks for the clear summary and the plan. Happy to coordinate. High level responses below and suggested next steps.

Snapshot & log retention (default):
- Full snapshots: retained 90 days by default for EU accounts (daily full + incremental).
- Incremental logs (operation/audit logs): retained 30 days by default; longer retention is an opt-in for audited customers.

Temporary exceptions / escrow options:
- We can provide a temporary audit-log escrow for up to 180 days for migrations that require regulatory hold; this is treated as an admin exception with paper trail + signed authorization from the customer PO.
- For your window we can set an exception starting 48 hours before the first migration step and lasting up to 120 days unless you request shorter.

Deletion / rollback workflow (summary):
1) Migration kicks off — snapshots are marked "migration-preserve" in metadata (no TTL).
2) If rollback requested within the pre-defined window, ops will restore from preserved snapshots (timeline ~2–8 hours depending on dataset size).
3) After the rollback window closes, snapshots enter a 30-day tombstone period before permanent purge; during tombstone we can still restore but require an escalation form.
4) Permanent deletion is irreversible after tombstone expiry; legal can request a further hold.

Compliance ask & DPA notes:
- We recommend formalizing the temporary escrow and extended log retention as an appendix to the DPA.
- I have attached our quick RBAC checklist and a short migration playbook for ops to align (RBAC-checklist.xlsx, migration-playbook.md).

Next steps:
- Proposed short sync: Tue Jul 6 10:00–10:30 UTC with Marcus (ops) and Kim (compliance) — does that work?
- If yes, send any DPA redline you plan to propose so Kim can pre-review.

Thanks — I’ll hold the slot if you confirm.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (555) 842-XXXX
attachments: RBAC-checklist.xlsx; migration-playbook.md

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Aaron Lee <support@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sequenced backup handoff for subprocessor rotation — retention & log exception asks

Thanks for the context — copying in Hannah from Legal since there will likely be DPA language about backup escrow and log retention. A couple of immediate compliance points to confirm before the sync: 

1) Scope of "audit-log escrow": please confirm exact artifacts you expect (full access logs vs application-level traces). Our standard escrow includes server access logs + API call metadata; application payloads are excluded unless explicitly requested and contractually allowed.

2) EU log retention carve-out: Redwood can support a temporary exception but we need a documented retention end-date and a PO or signed authorization from CloudBridge. We cannot accept open-ended requests.

3) KV/ML cache and ephemeral stores: these are cleared on snapshot purge. If you need preserved cache data for rollback, we need that explicitly listed and it will require an exception to our data minimization policy.

DPA redline preview: I will prepare a short redline to the DPA that: (a) enumerates the escrow artifacts; (b) sets a maximum 180-day escrow default; and (c) defines a 30-day tombstone period post-rollback-window before irreversible deletion. I will circulate a PDF (proposed-dpa-redline.pdf) before the call.

Quoted for context:
> Mina Haddad wrote:
> > Snapshot & log retention (default):
> > - Full snapshots: retained 90 days by default for EU accounts (daily full + incremental).
> > - Incremental logs (operation/audit logs): retained 30 days by default; longer retention is an opt-in for audited customers.

We should also confirm whether CloudBridge procurement requires an SLA exception for restore speed during the window. Marcus, can you confirm ops capacity for a potential ramp?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
attachments: proposed-dpa-redline.pdf

From: Aaron Lee <support@cloudbridge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sequenced backup handoff for subprocessor rotation — retention & log exception asks

Kim / Mina — appreciate the quick replies and the detailed controls. Quick answers from our side:
- Escrow artifacts: we need server access logs + API call metadata and a 90-day copy of application-level trace logs for a narrow set of services (payment and audit pipelines). We will supply a list of services before the meeting.
- Authorization: procurement will sign the PO and include the retention exception clause; expect DocuSign by EOD Mon Jul 6.
- SLA: procurement will request a one-off restore SLA for the weekend window — we can include that in the addendum.

We confirm Tue Jul 6 10:00–10:30 UTC for the sync. I will bring the detailed service list and the procurement rep will be on.

Thanks,
Aaron
CloudBridge — Cloud Ops
